input.rationale: Continued the decision-formation axis after the configuration-visibility result: the safety core is which acknowledgements may advance the leader's commit index and therefore reach the FSM. Reading the actual producers (leader setup, configuration change, quorum and lease helpers, replication startup, commitment, processLogs) shows a single consistent eligibility rule: only servers with Suffrage Voter appear in the commitment match set, so a Nonvoter/Staging acknowledgement is recorded by the replication goroutine's commitment.match call but is dropped by the map lookup, and a Nonvoter's reported index can never decide commitIndex. The same voter-only set governs the election/lease quorum. This turn also ran a race-enabled subset of the snapshot's own tests over configuration-change and leadership-transfer paths (TestRaft_LeadershipTransfer, TestRaft_AddVoter/AddNonvoter/DemoteVoter/RemoveServer, TestRaft_LeaderLease, TestRaft_ConfigChange) with no data race and no failure, which removes the cheap concurrency-defect hypothesis for those paths. No defect is asserted; the new investigation is a sourced question with a discriminator for a next experiment.

investigations.question: Can a Nonvoter's or Staging server's acknowledgement advance the leader's commitIndex (or reach the FSM), and is leader commit eligibility computed over the same participant set that the leader replicates to?
investigations.hypothesis: Leader commit eligibility is defined only over Voter entries of the current latest configuration, while replication state is created for every configured server; therefore a Nonvoter acknowledgement is silently dropped and cannot commit an entry, so FSM application never depends on non-voter support.
investigations.discriminator: In one process build a cluster whose latest configuration contains two Voters and one Nonvoter, make both Voters unable to store a new entry while the Nonvoter can (or conversely confirm that commits proceed when only a non-voter is lagging); commitIndex/apply progress must track Voter acknowledgements only. Withholding both Voter acknowledgements must stall commit and FSM application indefinitely, while withholding only the Nonvoter must not.

knowledge.statement: On the leader, the commit set is built exclusively from servers whose Suffrage is Voter: newCommitment and commitment.setConfiguration insert a matchIndexes entry only for Voter servers, commitment.match updates an index only if the reporting server is already a key in matchIndexes, and recalculate takes the majority-order element of those values. Replication goroutines, by contrast, are started for every server in configurations.latest regardless of suffrage, and quorumSize and checkLeaderLease also count only Voters. Consequently an acknowledgement from a Nonvoter/Staging server cannot advance commitIndex, and processLogs applies to the FSM only entries up to the leader's commitIndex.
knowledge.conditions: Leader state; protocol version 3 configuration with mixed suffrage; the leader's commitment was built from configurations.latest at leader setup and rebuilt on each committed/appended configuration change.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only account of the commit-eligibility rule. The three places that could let non-voter support count are all closed: the match set is built from Voter entries only at leader setup and at configuration change; match() rejects any server ID absent from that map, so a Nonvoter's AppendEntries response cannot create an entry; and recalculate derives commitIndex solely from the surviving map values. Replication is nonetheless started for every configured server, which explains why non-voters receive and store logs without ever contributing to commitment. No contradiction was found in the enclosing paths: the leader lease and election quorum helpers count the same Voter set, and processLogs is bounded by the leader's commitIndex. This is a source-explained negative, so no defect is asserted and the corresponding discriminator is left for execution rather than being inferred from the reading.
limitations: Source-only account: no retained execution yet exercises a mixed Voter/Nonvoter configuration, so the claim rests on reading the producers, not on an observed endpoint.
The reading covers the leader-side commit rule; it does not evaluate non-voter participation in any other mechanism (for example snapshot install or leadership transfer targeting a non-voter).

investigations.question: After a stable leader returns success from AddVoter, can a pre-existing voter's locally reported configuration remain without the new voter, and if so for how long under normal in-process operation?
investigations.hypothesis: The leader sets its own latest configuration and the commitment voter set immediately at append time, so a successful AddVoter only certifies a quorum of the new configuration, not that every pre-existing voter has observed the entry.
investigations.discriminator: Run the two-voter + one-new-server AddVoter scenario in-process and sample each node's reported configuration immediately after the future returns; disagreement should be transient and bounded by replication, versus persisting if the follower's configuration update path is broken.

knowledge.statement: On the leader, appendConfigurationEntry stores the new configuration log entry via dispatchLogs, then sets r.configurations.latest to the new configuration and calls commitment.setConfiguration(new), which rebuilds the commit voter set and recalculates the commit index. Commit of later entries is therefore evaluated over the new configuration's voters, and the leader's own latest configuration is updated at append time rather than at commit time.
knowledge.conditions: Leader in Leader state; configurationChangeChIfStable gated (latestIndex == committedIndex and a commit of the current term already observed); protocolVersion 3 so the entry is a LogConfiguration; prevIndex match in nextConfiguration.

knowledge.statement: nextConfiguration's AddNonvoter case does not demote an existing member: if the server ID already exists with Suffrage other than Nonvoter, only its Address is updated and its Voter/Staging suffrage is retained; a new server is appended as Nonvoter. Demotion of an existing voter is only reachable through DemoteVoter.
knowledge.conditions: protocol-version-3 ID-based configuration change request with a client-supplied server ID that already exists in the current configuration.

knowledge.statement: On a follower, appendEntries stores accepted new entries and then calls processConfigurationLogEntry for each stored configuration entry, which sets configurations.latest/latestIndex to the newly decoded configuration at store time, before the entry's commit index is known. configurations.latest is therefore the locally stored (possibly uncommitted) configuration, and GetConfiguration on any node reports it without consulting the main thread.
knowledge.conditions: Follower receiving AppendEntries whose entries are new or whose conflicting suffix was deleted; protocol 3 LogConfiguration entries (or deprecated peer entries); configurations.latest is updated from the follower's own log store, independent of LeaderCommitIndex.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: the leader updates its own latest configuration and the commitment voter set at append time, and commitment is recomputed over the new voter set, so AddVoter success only means a quorum of the new configuration stored the entry. In an isolated native run of the submitted scenario the new configuration was already reported by all three nodes at the first sample (~1ms), i.e. no lasting disagreement. The earlier 'peer mismatch' occurred once during a full package run and did not reappear on a repeat run of the same suite. No source path was found that would keep a pre-existing voter's latest configuration permanently missing a committed configuration entry; the conflicting observation is currently attributed to harness timing under load, but that attribution is not yet grounded in a controller receipt.

Source reading already showed that the leader updates its own latest configuration and the commitment voter set at append time, so AddVoter success certifies only that a quorum of the new configuration stored the entry; combined with the follower-side behavior that latest configuration is set at log-store time, a pre-existing voter's reported configuration may legitimately lag the leader's by one replication delivery. The retained execution witnesses exactly that: the AddVoter future returned success at 2ms (index 1, err <nil>, index 3), the pre-existing voter server-d6f82acc reported num_servers=2/has_new_member=false at the same 2ms sample (index 3), and at 102ms the same server reported num_servers=3/has_new_member=true (index 6). All probes 6 through 91 (out to 2927ms) show 3 servers on that server, so the disagreement did not persist or recur within the observed window. The earlier unexplained 'peer mismatch' under full-suite load is thus consistent with the same bounded replication transient rather than a broken configuration-update path on pre-existing voters.
limitations: Single execution with two 100ms-spaced samples bracketing the transition: the exact instant the follower adopted the new configuration is only bounded to the interval (2ms, 102ms], so the observation shows boundedness, not a latency bound under load.
The sampled predicate is each node's locally reported latest configuration (getLatestConfiguration), not commit ordering; the samples say nothing about when the follower committed the entry.

The originally observed full-suite 'peer mismatch' lasted up to the harness 5s limit and was not reproduced in isolation, so its cause under CPU contention remains unmeasured; only its identity with this bounded transient is supported, not its duration.

Added the new investigation @q_nonvoter_commit with a mixed-suffrage discriminator, promoted the Fact @k_voter_only_commit, and interpreted it as explained with no defect asserted (source-only). Also ran a race-enabled subset of the snapshot's own tests over configuration-change and leadership-transfer paths (TestRaft_LeadershipTransfer, AddVoter/AddNonvoter/DemoteVoter/RemoveServer, LeaderLease, ConfigChange) with no data race and no failure.
